chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from some of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The sun does not rise on any day more superior than the day of Friday, and indeed the speech of the birds on it, when some of them meet others, is 'Peace, peace,' and it is a virtuous day."
ai.seo_question: What makes the day of Friday superior in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration underscores the cosmological significance of Friday, portraying it as the pinnacle of time where creation itself acknowledges its sanctity through the birds' salutations. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on Friday as a day of spiritual elevation and divine favor, linking natural phenomena to the metaphysical status of the day.
